chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the testimony (bayyinah) when it is established on the truth: Is it permissible for the judge to rule based on the word of the testimony without asking questions, if he does not know them? He said: 'Five things upon which people must act based on the apparent ruling are: guardianships/authorities, marriages, inheritances, slaughtering (of animals), and testimonies. So when its apparent aspect is apparent and trustworthy, its testimony is valid and it is not asked about its inner reality.'
ai.seo_question: What are the five areas where apparent status is sufficient for legal rulings in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *al-zuhur* (presumption of correctness), ruling that in five critical domains—guardianship, marriage, inheritance, slaughter, and testimony—the outward appearance of a person is sufficient for legal validity without probing their inner reality (*batin*). This doctrine facilitates social stability by allowing courts to rely on apparent truth (*zahir*) in the absence of specific knowledge about the individuals, reflecting the Shia juristic balance between legal certainty and spiritual depth.
